To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we were able to classify the specimen images with 100% accuracy at the species level using only 26 species, and (ii) we were able not only to classify the specimen into the correct species, but also to localize the specimen in the image, which is an important step towards automated identification of specimens.

the classification of herbarium specimens at the species level using computer vision is currently not possible with the available data and that the classification of specimens into a few broad categories, such as the 26 tree species used in this study, is possible with a high degree of accuracy.

(1) the classification of herbarium specimens into species categories using a Support Vector Machine is possible with an accuracy of 80.2%; (2) the accuracy of the classification increases with increasing number of training specimens; (3) the accuracy is highest for the most abundant species and lowest for the rarest species; (4) the accuracy is lower when the training set includes only specimens of the same herbarium than if it includes a larger number of herbaria.
